newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Oppenheimer & Co to take 30 pct of Bulgarian bank.
newsitem.headline: Oppenheimer & Co to take 30 pct of Bulgarian bank.

text.p: The U.S. Oppenheimer & Co., a subsidiary of Oppenheimer Group Inc., plans to take a stake of about 30 percent in state-owned United Bulgarian Bank (UBB) under a privatisation plan, the UBB said.
The Bank Consolidation Company, which now owns more than 98 percent of UBB, will offer its holding to Oppenheimer, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and state-owned Bulbank.

"Along with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Bulbank with 35 percent each, Oppenheimer & Co will be offered 30 percent from the new share issue of the UBB," said a UBB official, who declined to be named. The official gave no more details.
The new acquisitions will be voted at the UBB annual shareholders meeting, expected to be held on July 25 after the EBRD board approves its investment.
After that, the three investors will be offered the same size stakes in a new $30 million share issue.
So far the UBB's capital totalled 21.07 billion levs.
BCC, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, boosted UBB capital through $119 million of domestic bad loan bonds last year.
In line with changes in the bank's ownership, the UBB will abolish its two-tier management system comprising supervisory and executive boards and will replace it by a nine-member board of directors.

The nine-member board formed through nominees of all three major shareholders will be authorised to decide on a further capital increase through a new share issue of up to $15 million in the next two years, said the official.
The UBB was set up in 1992 through a merger of 22 smaller banking institutions and is expected to be the first privatisation project implemented by the BCC.
In line with the pledges to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Bulgaria plans to privatise all six operating state-owned banks by mid-1998. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
